newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Creditanstalt will be off the shelves soon - Klima.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt will be off the shelves soon - Klima.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima stressed on Tuesday that Creditanstalt, which has topped the government's privatisation list for six years, would be off the shelves before its year-end sell-by date.
"I want to have a decision on the sale this year," Klima told journalists after the regular weekly cabinet meeting, reiterating earlier statements.
The minister added that he had received three indicative offers for the government's 70 percent voting stake in the country's flagship bank, of which he had rejected one as insufficient.
The two remaining bidders would now be allowed to take part in the due diligence process, expected to start soon.
A consortium led by Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali, which includes German, Italian and Belgian banks, is the only known bidder for the bank. No details of the other bidder have emerged.

Austrian newspapers have repeatedly mentioned several U.S. banks, among them Citibank, BankAmerica and GE Capital, a unit of General Electric, as possible suitors, but none of the rumours have ever been confirmed.
